key_facts: Symptoms include palpitations, fatiguability, bipedal edema, weight loss, and diarrhea

Pulmonary artery systolic pressure is 77 mm Hg

shortlist.label: Hyperthyroidism due to Graves' disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has symptoms of hyperthyroidism, including palpitations, weight loss, and diarrhea, with laboratory tests showing low TSH and high free T4 levels, and the presence of thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor antibody

shortlist.label: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is in rapid atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of 170 beats/min, which is a life-threatening condition requiring immediate attention

shortlist.label: Pulmonary embolism
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has bilateral lower-lobe acute pulmonary emboli on CT pulmonary angiogram, which is a life-threatening condition requiring immediate anticoagulation

shortlist.label: Intracardiac thrombus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has multiple intracardiac thrombi in the left atrial appendage, posterior mitral leaflet, right ventricular outflow tract, and proximal pulmonary artery, which increases the risk of further thromboembolic events

shortlist.label: Cardiomyopathy due to hyperthyroidism
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has biventricular enlargement, left atrial dilatation, and severe mitral and tricuspid regurgitation on echocardiography, which may be related to hyperthyroidism-induced cardiomyopathy
